YMCA BULLETIN, 13 FEBRUARY 1970 — A NATIONAL REPRINT OF THE KANAWANA SKI ITEM
Internet Archive identifier: bulletin-1970-02-13 | creator: YMCA of Montreal
Collections: ymca-montreal-fonds, rma-concordia-publications | 4,164 characters
Found 2026-09-07 by the accounted sweep of rma-concordia-publications (p_479).

WHAT THIS IS, AND WHY IT IS NOT A DUPLICATE OF SOMETHING ALREADY HELD.

The Kanawana passage in it is already in this wiki, word for word, in
traditions/winter-programming.md, from the Montreal YMCA's bilingual communiqué
of 29 JANUARY 1970 (src_ymf_p0145_news_release_1970_01_29). The destination was
checked before any of this was written and the passage was found there, in
detail, under the heading "Winter 1969-70: a family ski day, already full".

WHAT IS NEW IS NOT THE CONTENT BUT THE REACH. This is a different document,
issued a fortnight later, and it is national. Its masthead reads "for
information / all staff / key lay persons / BULLETIN", and its other items are
National Council business: the Annual Meeting of 21-24 May at the new National
Capital YMCA-YWCA, 180 Argyle Avenue, Ottawa; appointments of representative
members "according to procedure outlined in February 3 memo by Les Vipond";
binding details available "through National Council's Records Office"; car cards
"now available through National YMCA Supplies Office"; and an enclosure of the
Montreal Residence's bilingual folder and rate card.

TWO EDITORIAL DECISIONS ARE VISIBLE IN THE REPRINT AND BOTH ARE WORTH KEEPING.

1. "West Island Branch (Montreal)". The parenthesis is added. The Montreal
   communiqué needed no such gloss; a bulletin going to all staff and key lay
   persons across the country did. That parenthesis is the evidence that the
   readership is national.

2. THE NATIONAL EDITOR TOOK THE SKI ITEM AND LEFT THE STAFF APPOINTMENT. The
   29 January communiqué carries, immediately before the soup item, "TURNER TO
   KANAWANA: Jim Turner, associate executive of the amalgamated operations of
   West Island and Lachine-Dorval Branches, will be the on-site director and
   head of program at Kamp Kanawana this summer." The 13 February bulletin does
   not reprint it. So the national office judged an oversubscribed family ski
   day at a Montreal camp to be of interest to YMCAs across Canada, and the
   appointment of that camp's director not to be.

THE PASSAGE AS PRINTED HERE, transcribed complete:

  "IT'S MAINLY BECAUSE OF THE SOUP: West Island Branch (Montreal) seems to have
  come up with a real winner. Its family ski program, running Saturdays at Kamp
  Kanawana, just can't handle anybody else. Here's the package. A network of
  cross-country trails. Firmly-packed hills for downhill runs and instructions.
  Skiing lessons. A well-equipped nursery, supervised by experienced baby
  sitters. Facilities for preparing lunch, Free soup."

Otherwise identical to the January text, including the last comma splice before
"Free soup." The January OCR has "just ean't handle" where this has "can't"; the
scan, not the printer.

NULL RESULTS. "Kanawana" occurs once in the bulletin, in this item. "Otoreke" 0,
"Perrot" 0, "Voyageurs" 0. No other Kanawana or camping material.
